text:
megan.peopleops: Quick Q from events team: we shipped a 35lb box of conference swag to the hotel for the booth. Hotel billed a $45 handling fee + $12/day storage for two days on the final folio. We used the company card for the label but the hotel charged incidentals to the event lead's card during check-in. Are handling + short-term storage fees reimbursable? Any docs we should attach other than the hotel folio and shipper tracking?

sarah.events: Context: box arrived two days before the team, hotel put it in back storage and then to the booth on setup day. The shipper (DHL) tracking shows delivered and signed by "bell staff". We prepaid shipping on corp card; the hotel still charged handling.

josh.finance: Policy short answer: vendor fees directly tied to running a company event (handling, drayage, short-term storage) are reimbursable if documented. Two requirements: 1) itemized hotel folio showing the handling/storage line items, and 2) proof of delivery (tracking + POD or signatory). If the hotel charged an individual card in error, finance will re-bill it to the company card once we have the folio + note from hotel.

megan.peopleops: Good to know. The event lead paid at check-in because the hotel front desk insisted on a card. Hotel said they'd reverse it if we provide billing instructions. Do we need a manager approval to re-bill?

josh.finance: Manager approval (events lead's manager) is enough for internal approval. Also include a brief attestation: "Box for Redwood booth, delivered to hotel on 2025-09-25; fee charged to personal card by hotel; please re-bill to company." Finance will create a chargeback. If the hotel refuses a reversal, we'll reimburse the employee after manager signoff and proof.

hotel-billing-bot: hotel folio uploaded: 2187659900_hilton-sfo-folio.pdf

receipts-bot: tracking uploaded: 2187659920_DHL-TRACK-1234567890.pdf

sarah.events: One wrinkle: the folio has a single line "Handling fee" $57 and a separate tax. It doesn't say "storage" or provide days. Will that be a problem?

josh.finance: Not ideal but acceptable. If the folio doesn't itemize per-day storage, add a short note in the expense report describing arrival/check-in/setup dates and reference the tracking POD. Finance may ask the hotel to provide a breakdown; if hotel can't, we still accept the documented fee if manager approves.

megan.peopleops: Also asked: can we avoid this in future by adding billing instructions on shipment label (bill-to: Redwood Inference, Attn: Events Billing) and by contacting hotel events team prior to delivery? Any template?

sarah.events: Yes. Best practice: 1) include a billing instruction label, 2) email the hotel's events manager with shipper ETA and ask for receiving/storage handling waiver or to bill master account, 3) if personal card is requested at check-in, ask for a temporary authorization and note we will provide corporate folio. I have a short email template I can paste.

josh.finance: Also note: for large drayage or multi-box shipments, use our preferred vendors (listed in procurement) — they have negotiated hotel handling waivers. For one-off swag boxes, this approach is fine.

megan.peopleops: Thanks. I'll attach the folio + tracking + manager approval in the expense report and mark it "events - shipping handling fee - re-bill request". Will follow up if hotel refuses reversal. :thumbsup:
